subject: ISV marketplace slate — commission split, lead ownership, and co-sell play
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily@optiscale.io>, OptiScale Partnerships <partnerships@optiscale.io>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: ISV marketplace slate — commission split, lead ownership, and co-sell play

Hi Emily / OptiScale team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited by how tightly OptiScale's connector can reduce onboarding time for our shared customers. Attached is a short draft that outlines a proposed marketplace commercial slate and lead-handling guardrails so we can move toward a signed pilot before the quarter close. Top-line items: 

- Commission: tiered marketplace fee + referral credit. We propose a baseline 12% platform fee on net ARR for marketplace-originated deals, with an extra 6% referral credit to the ISV for the first 12 months when OptiScale is the introducing party and is active on the opportunity.
- Tier breakpoints: 0–25k, 25k–100k, 100k+. Sliding increases for larger deals (we've called this out in the doc).
- Lead registration window: 90 days by default; we can consider extensions for enterprise co-sell motions.
- Co-sell obligations: OptiScale to provide technical pre-sales support for integrations (1 SME on call for pilot deals) and Redwood will provide joint demo credits and a 60-day onboarding credit for pilot customers.
- Exclusivity: none on general categories; we can discuss short-term exclusivity on jointly-marketed pilots if there is a mutual commitment.

Questions for you: are the tier breakpoints workable? Would OptiScale expect a longer lead-registration window for larger enterprise accounts? Any regulatory or procurement constraints we should know about (PO timelines, distributor involvement)?

If that looks directionally right I can loop in legal and send a one-page term sheet. Are you available for a quick 30-min sync tomorrow or early next week?

Attachments: redwood-isv-marketplace-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF, ~180KB)

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai | x4721

From: Emily Park <emily@optiscale.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: OptiScale Partnerships <partnerships@optiscale.io>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ISV marketplace slate — commission split, lead ownership, and co-sell play

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the clear proposal and the draft. A few clarifying points from our side so we can prepare internal numbers before the call:

- Commission math: for our commercial model, OptiScale typically expects 18–20% for first-year ARR on partner-originated deals above $100k, because of the higher cost to acquire and integrate enterprise accounts. For smaller deals (<25k) 8–10% is typical. Can we do a parameterized approach (e.g., X% first year, Y% year two)?
- Lead registration window: we often ask for 180 days for larger accounts due to elongated procurement cycles; 90 days is OK for SMBs but will be a tough sell for our BD team on enterprise.
- Attribution: what systems will Redwood accept for registration? Ideally HubSpot+signed MQL sheet or a Salesforce opportunity marked as partner-introduced.
- Exclusivity: we won't accept full exclusivity, but will consider time-bound pilot exclusivity if Redwood commits to co-marketing and demand-gen credits.

Couple of asks before a legal review: can you share a one-pager term sheet and a sample SLA/SSO/SOC2 evidence pack we can pass to our procurement?

On timing — I can do a 30-min sync Mon 9/28 10am PT or Tue 9/29 11am PT. Which works?

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ISV marketplace slate — internal notes and recommended counter

Jasmine / Ben — internal view and suggested counter for OptiScale:

Key principles I used: protect platform unit economics, be generous on pilot economics to land GTM momentum, and standardize registration to be low-friction.

Proposed counter (summary):
- Tiered commission to align with OptiScale ask but cap first-year uplift: 18% for >100k first-year ARR (paid as 12% platform fee + 6% referral bonus), 12% for 25k–100k (8% + 4%), 6% for <25k (6% single platform fee, no extra bonus).
- Lead registration: 120 days default, extendable to 180 days for named enterprise pursuits with a joint intake form.
- Attribution: HubSpot + signed referral form OR Salesforce opportunity flagged partner-introduced + link to original contact email thread. No manual spreadsheets unless both parties sign off.
- Onboarding credit: $5k for first pilot production customer (applies to integration work and demo credits).
- Compliance pack: attach SOC2 summary, SSO integration notes, and a sample commercial term sheet.

I attached a short partner playbook that maps handoffs (BD -> Solutions -> CS) and a draft term sheet. If we go with the above we can offer to OptiScale a 30-day exclusivity on co-marketed pilots for any jointly-backed deals >100k, conditioned on a signed LOI.

Attachments: partner-playbook-draft.xlsx (Workbook, 45KB)

Happy to jump on the call; I can cover the commercial pieces and Ben can cover billing/ops.

—Camila
Director, Partner GTM | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ISV marketplace slate — commission split, lead ownership, and co-sell play

Emily — thanks for the quick reply and for surfacing OptiScale's expectations. Based on internal review (Camila + Ben) we've put together the attached counter and a short one-page term sheet to accelerate legal review. High level:

- We can accommodate the higher enterprise uplift (18% first-year for >100k) as a combination of platform fee + referral bonus, but we need that capped to first-year to protect long-term economics.
- We'll move the default registration window to 120 days and allow a 180-day extension for named enterprise pursuits (requires joint intake).
- Attribution: HubSpot or Salesforce as primary sources + a signed referral form for large deals.
- Pilot exclusivity: happy to offer a 30-day co-marketing exclusivity for joint pilots >100k if OptiScale executes an LOI and commits to a co-marketing plan.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick sync — Mon 9/28 10am PT (Emily selected) — calendar invite to follow.
2) I will drop the one-page term sheet in DocuSign for approvals after we align on the few bullets above.
3) Camila will send the partner playbook and sample compliance pack to your procurement after the call.

Attached: redwood-isv-term-sheet-draft.docx (Docx, ~28KB)
